sentences.text:
An FIR, under Sections 376, 328, 506, 120-B of IPC and Section 66A of the IT Act,
was registered against the petitioner on 23.10.2021, at Police Station Pachokhar,
District Firozabad.

The petitioner was released on bail by the High Court in that case vide an order dated 16.02.2022.
2.

The petitioner allegedly, in misuse of the concession of bail, started threatening the victim and her family members so much so that the younger sister of the victim, who was a minor, committed suicide allegedly due to the threats extended by the petitioner.

Consequently, Case Crime No.656/2022, under Section 306 IPC, was registered against the petitioner on 01.10.2022 at Police Station Tundla, District Firozabad, on the complaint made by the father of the victims.
The petitioner was arrested very next day, i.e., 02.10.2022 and is in custody since then.

He applied for bail and the High Court, vide impugned order dated 23.04.2024, declined to release the petitioner on bail after taking notice of the allegations that the petitioner along with one unknown person had stopped the deceased in the way, abused and mis-behaved with her and then threatened with dire consequences.

3. While issuing notice in the petition on 01.10.2024, the Trial Court was directed to record the statements of parents of the deceased victim in the case under Section 376 IPC etc. on the date fixed,
i.e. 05.10.2024.
The direction was issued with the object that possibility of extension of threat to the vital witnesses could be ruled out.
Meanwhile, the father of the victims has also joined these proceedings as a complainant.
4. We have heard learned counsel for the parties, including learned counsel for the complainant, and carefully perused the material placed on record.
5. It is an admitted fact that the statements of the victim girl and her parents in the 2021 case under Section 376 IPC etc. have already been recorded.
Similarly, the statements of the parents of the victim girl, the suicide of whom led to registration of a case under Section 306 IPC, have been recorded in that case also.
Learned counsel informed that there are 28 witnesses in the case under Section 376 IPC and there are 22 witnesses proposed to be examined in the later case under Section 306 IPC.
The conclusion of trial will, thus, take some reasonable time.
That being so, and without expressing any views on merit of the case, we direct that the petitioner be released on bail, subject to his furnishing bail bonds to the satisfaction of the Trial Court.

6. In addition, the following conditions are imposed on the petitioner:
(i) He shall report fortnightly in the Police Station at Tundla, District Firozabad, for ascertainment of his good behaviour.

(ii) If the petitioner or any person associated with him is found indulging in extending threat to the victim, in the case under Section 376 IPC, or to her parents/close relatives, it shall be taken as a misuse of concession of bail.

sentences.text:
(iii) The petitioner is a resident of village Nagla Jaat, Post Pamari, Police Station Pachokhara, District Firozabad whereas the victims family resides in Indira Nagar,
Tundla Chauraha, Tundla, District Firozabad.
That being so, the petitioner is directed not to be seen in the locality where the victims family resides till the conclusion of trial.
(iv) The petitioner shall appear before the Trial Court regularly.
(v) The petitioner shall extend full cooperation to the Trial Court in all the cases pending against him.
(vi) The Trial Court is directed to expedite the trial in the Section 376 IPC matter and conclude the same within six months.
If the Petitioner does not co-operate, the Presiding Officer shall send a report to this Court, whereupon the instant bail order can be recalled.
7. The State of Uttar Pradesh or the victims family shall be at liberty to approach the competent court under Section 220 Cr.P.C. for clubbing of the trial in the three cases.
Such an application, if filed, shall be considered as per its own merit.
8. The Special Leave Petition stands disposed of in the above terms.
9. As a result, the pending interlocutory applications also stand disposed of.

(SATISH KUMAR YADAV) (PREETHI T.C.)
